articleTitle: Investigation and Multi-response Optimization of Process Parameters of Electrical Discharge Machining on H21 Steel Using GRA-TOPSISCRITIC Method
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Mechatronics, Control and Robotics (ICMCR)
abstract: The efficiency of optimizing numerous response parameters of electrical discharge machining (EDM) is investigated in this study with the assistance of grey relational analysis (GRA) and the approach for the order of preference by similarity to the ideal solution (TOPSIS) coupled with the criteria importance through criteria inter-correlation (CRITIC) method. The study considered polarity, peak current, electrode material, pulse-on time $\left(T_{\text {on }}\right)$, pulse-off time $\left(T_{\text {off }}\right)$, electrode material, polarity, and dielectric as the machining process parameters (MPPs) while using material subtraction rate (MSR), surface roughness, and tool degradation rate (TGR) as response parameters. First, Taguchi’s L18-OA was used to execute the experiments, and the response parameters were then recorded. The analysis of variance (ANOVA) was carried out to determine the influential MPP with 95% confidence level. The findings indicate that the optimal parametric settings were $2 \mathrm{~A}$ peak current, $60 \mu \mathrm{s} \mathrm{T}_{\text {on }}, 60 \mu \mathrm{s} \mathrm{T}_{\text {off }}$, copper electrode material, reverse polarity, and distilled water dielectric using the GRA-CRITIC method, and $4 \mathrm{~A}$ peak current, $30 \mu \mathrm{s} \mathrm{T}_{\text {on }}, 20 \mu \mathrm{s} \mathrm{T}_{\text {off, brass electrode, }}$, reverse polarity, and kerosene dielectric using TOPSIS CRITIC. The Peak current was found to be the most influential MPP, contributing 25.19% to the performance measures, followed by $\mathbf{T}_{\text {on }}, \mathbf{T}_{\text {off }}$, electrode material, polarity, and dielectric, contributing $24.45 \%, 13.42 \% ; 13.04 \%, 9.45 \%$, and 6.23%, respectively. Furthermore, the ANOVA of preference values revealed that $T_{\text {off }}$ had the maximum influence on performance measures, contributing 24.55% of the performance measures, followed by peak current $(16.30 \%)$, polarity $(10.67 \%), \mathrm{T}_{\text {on }}(6.67 \%)$, electrode material $(4.57 \%)$, and dielectric fluid $(6.57 \%)$. Confirmatory tests were run on the derived optimal values, and the findings indicated that the final improvements in the preference and grey grade values were 0.008016 and 0.006728, respectively. In addition, regression analysis was performed to evaluate the relation among the machining variables.

articleTitle: Simulation Analysis of Pulsation Characteristics of Axial Piston Pump
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Mechatronics, Control and Robotics (ICMCR)
abstract: The emergence of “digital hydraulic” makes many industrial fields put forward higher requirements for the performance of piston water pump, and realizes the control of piston water pump, and realizes the digital control of it. But because the efficiency of hydraulic drive is not high, to carry out a wide range of adjustment, need to go through the complex mechanical energy - hydraulic energy conversion, so the efficiency is very high, pressure loss is also very large. Therefore, taking a new type of double row piston pump with flow distribution as an example, the pulsation characteristics of axial piston pump are theoretically analyzed, and the flow pulsation and capacity utilization are simulated by computer. The simulation results show that the closed-loop and integration of components continue to improve, components can be modular assembly, easy maintenance, clean appearance, smaller volume, less pipeline connection, can effectively prevent leakage and pipeline loss caused by too many pipeline interfaces. It can be seen that the control method based on fast switching valve controlled pump effectively promotes the improvement of flow pulsation and capacity utilization.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Control Design Based on Zone Barrier Lyapunov Function
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Mechatronics, Control and Robotics (ICMCR)
abstract: This paper investigates the control design for nonlinear systems with output constraint, according to a safe set from mathematical understanding or zone stability from an engineering point of view, and the corresponding zone Barrier Lyapunov Function (zBLF) stability analysis. The novel constraint function is provided to allow the output state to travel freely in the predefined zone meanwhile not transgress the barrier area. To articulate the area-keeping problem, we first propose the zone stability to a second SISO nonlinear system. Next, zBLF in asymmetric form is developed into a class of nonlinear systems in the strict feedback form. The stability analysis of the zone Barrier Lyapunov function is to ensure that the output does not break free of the restricted constraint while simultaneously ensuring that the states remain free within the admissible set. As a result, control theory expands its range of applications and contributes to its application development. The actual system does not need to do additional work to achieve the state constraint. Finally, the numerical example is conducted to illustrate the zBLF features and further explorations of the merits are carried out to showcase the effectiveness.

articleTitle: UAMDynCon-DT: A Data-driven Dynamics and Robust Control Framework for UAM Vehicle Digitalization using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Mechatronics, Control and Robotics (ICMCR)
abstract: This study presents a data-driven dynamics and robust control framework, referred to as UAMDynCon-DT, for the accurate cloning of ground-truth dynamics and the robust control of attitude in a personal aerial vehicle (PAV) known as the KP-1 eVTOL aircraft. The proposed framework utilizes exponentially stabilizing control Lyapunov functions to ensure stability and robustness, and utilizes a nonlinear flight dynamics model of the KP-1 to construct the controller. To evaluate its performance, real-world flight tests were conducted on a scaled model of the KP-1, and results were compared to those obtained from traditional control methods. The tests demonstrated improved resilience to disturbances and uncertainties when utilizing the proposed framework. This research suggests that UAMDynConDT could be a valuable tool for the future development of large-scale urban air mobility vehicles.

articleTitle: Course-Tracking of Multiple Fault Cases of a Model Scaled Surface Vessel with Feedback Linearization
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Mechatronics, Control and Robotics (ICMCR)
abstract: In this paper, the fault tolerant control with priory using feedback linearization and PID controller of a model scaled container vessel is proposed. First, the nonlinear mathematical model for a model scaled vessel equipped with propulsion configuration of single rudder and two thrusters are presented. Then, the control system based on feedback linearization is developed for different cases of the actuator failure, including the failure of a rudder and a thruster separately. Lastly, the timedomain simulation is conducted to evaluate the performance of feedback linearization control in path following problems as the vessel experiencing normal operation as well as propulsion system failure. The results present that the vessel can manoeuvre along the desired circle and zigzag trajectories. This paper contributes to the development of control system for autonomous surface vessel by providing an approach for fault tolerant control to be applied in emergency operations.

articleTitle: Mathematical Model Analysis and Control Strategy
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Mechatronics, Control and Robotics (ICMCR)
abstract: Liquid level control is widely used in steel, petrochemical, food filling, pharmaceutical, power plant and other industries, and is an important part of industrial automation. The three tank level height control system is a kind of multi input and multi output control object, which has the characteristics of nonlinearity, time-varying, large inertia, hysteresis and coupling. The in-depth and detailed mathematical model construction and control scheme design can provide a basis for the design of further experimental devices and experimental schemes. Based on the three tank interconnected water tank, this paper designs a liquid level height control system, analyzes the mathematical model of the water tank system, and studies the control strategy for the three tank interconnected SISO water tank system, which improves the control level of the system and can be applied to general industrial control systems. It has more extensive application value and higher practical significance.

articleTitle: Design of a Control System for GreyWater Collection and Reuse in Toilet Tanks
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Mechatronics, Control and Robotics (ICMCR)
abstract: A very concurrent problem is the water scarcity that is growing day by day because many of us misuse water resources. Therefore, this research has an alternative solution which is the reuse of greywater (GW) which is extracted from hand washers, showers, and washing machines, which will go through a process of filtering and disinfection using UV rays for subsequent reuse through an automated ON-OFF control system. In this research, the VDI 2221 methodology will be carried out in which the design processes are applied to manufacture new systems, such as control improvements, among others. The software Tia Portal and Factory IO were used to visualize the sensors and actuators that simulate the filtering and filling of GW. Finally, it is concluded that the application of a control and automated system for the reuse of GW is of great importance to improve and optimize the use of water and thus reduce water scarcity in different parts of the world.

articleTitle: SLAM-DRLnav: A SLAM-Enhanced Deep Reinforcement Learning Navigation Framework for Indoor Self-driving
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Mechatronics, Control and Robotics (ICMCR)
abstract: This work proposes a new framework for mobile robot navigation that combines two existing methods - SLAM and DRL - to enhance performance. Instead of relying solely on SLAM for mapping and location, or solely on DRL for path planning, the proposed framework utilizes both techniques in conjunction. Specifically, it utilizes SLAM for creating maps and determining the robot’s location, while using an ACO algorithm to generate a static path plan. In dynamic environments with moving obstacles, the framework employs DRL-based local path planning. Additionally, the proposed framework compares and evaluates the performance of three different DRL-based navigation algorithms - DGN, TD3, and PPO. Overall, the goal of this framework is to improve the localization and path planning capabilities of mobile robots in dynamic environments.

articleTitle: An Investigation into Bark Detachment Disease in Tree Trunks Using Different GPR Antennas and Frequency Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Mechatronics, Control and Robotics (ICMCR)
abstract: Trees are broadly considered major natural and socio-economical assets. Their protection and safeguarding must be therefore a priority. The bark is well known as being the first protective layer of a tree trunk, and monitoring thickness and potential areas of detachment is crucial for tree preservation purposes. Direct methods (e.g., sampling) may cause local damage that eventually can extend to the whole tree. To this effect, this research aims at investigating the possibility to extract information from the Ground Penetrating Radar (GPR) technique regarding tree bark thickness estimation and detachment occurrences. Given the relatively contained thickness of tree barks, their estimation is a challenging task. Different GPR antennas and frequency systems (1.5, 2 and 4 GHz) are therefore used to collect data on a tree log affected by bark detachment. Time-domain signals and their frequency spectra are therefore analysed and compared each to one another. Results show reliable indication of time-zero amplitude location on the bark and prove the capabilities of high-frequency GPR systems to effectively detect the bark thickness in bark-detached trunk sections.

articleTitle: Research on the Optimization of Prefabricated Electromechanical Installation Process Using Artificial Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Mechatronics, Control and Robotics (ICMCR)
abstract: In recent years, advanced information technology, network technology, Internet of Things technology, cloud computing technology and so on are developing rapidly, which has played an important role in promoting the development and reform of the society. The application of these advanced intelligent technology in mechanical and electrical engineering has greatly improved the quality of the project while reducing the construction cost. Mechanical and electrical installation and construction has an important impact on the economic benefits of enterprises. Mechanical and electrical installation engineering has many equipment types and involves many professional fields, so we should fully master the mechanical and electrical installation technology to ensure targeted construction, so as to comprehensively improve the project progress. Firstly, this paper briefly describes the prefabricated board installation process and optimization method. Secondly, the prefabricated mechanical and electrical installation process in intelligent engineering is optimized by using the characteristics of artificial intelligence. Finally, the practical application proves that the flexible use of prefabricated installation and construction technology in the installation and construction process of intelligent mechanical and electrical machinery is beneficial to saving resources and energy, improving labor production efficiency and quality and safety level.

articleTitle: Rockwell Hardness Standard Machine in the Form of Force Sensor with Automatic Point Selection Function
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Mechatronics, Control and Robotics (ICMCR)
abstract: On the basis of intelligent measurement, this paper introduces a Rockwell hardness standard machine that uses high-precision force sensor to load and has the function of automatic selection of dots. A closed-loop control system is developed, The hardware consists of a servo motor, a reducer and a ball screw through sprocket drive. The software adopts PLC control, so that the loading rate is stable and meets the requirements of the regulations; a two-dimensional mobile platform is developed to automatically replace the measurement points on the hardness block, so as to achieve uniform distribution of indentation. The standard machine can realize real-time monitoring of force value and indentation depth during loading, so as to better analyze the change of force value and indentation during Rockwell hardness block verification. The test results show that the initial test error force meets ± 0.2%, the total test force error meets ± 0.1%, and the repeatability of the standard machine also meets the requirements of the regulation.

articleTitle: Neural Networks Based Road-Tire Friction Coefficient Estimation Using Fiala Tire Model and Kalman Filter
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Mechatronics, Control and Robotics (ICMCR)
abstract: In this paper an algorithm for friction coefficient estimation is presented by using the robotic system dynamic model and feed forward neural networks (FFNN). The system is a robotic vehicle with articulated suspension (RVAS). The Fiala tire model is investigated and modeled. Then the road and robotic vehicle data is generated that represent the working environment required for neural networks training and validation. The input and output data pairs are prepared to estimate the road tire friction coefficient based on the inputs of tire forces (longitudinal, lateral, and vertical), slip angle, slip ratio, and wheel angular speed. The data is divided into two parts, one for training and the other for validation. For each FFNN design (number of neurons), the training process is repeated 50 times for each design to ensure error saturation. The training and validation tests are executed based on the root mean square error (RMSE) as the main performance measure. It is found that a FFNN of size 19 neurons can estimate the road tire friction coefficient effectively. The training results RMSE 12.87% and validation results RMSE 13.09%. Moreover, a detailed study of the uncertainties effect is executed up to 30% of each input to the FFNN.

articleTitle: Trail Control of Bicycle for Improving Stability and Maneuverability
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Mechatronics, Control and Robotics (ICMCR)
abstract: The purpose of this study is to improve the stability and maneuverability of bicycles by controlling the trail effect according to the riding conditions of the bicycle. An experimental system is developed, and experiments are conducted to investigate the changes in bicycle behavior occurring due to the variation at the trail effect when the offset is varied. First, the bicycle behavior with different offsets is investigated by bicycle simulator. To verify the behavior depending on the size of the offset experimentally, we utilize the experimental bicycle for analysis in which the position of the offset can be changed in steps. As a result, a stable offset position at a speed of 10 km/h is confirmed by running experiments. A steer-by-wire mechanism bicycle, in which the handlebars and front wheel are mechanically separated and the front wheel can be electrically controlled without giving extra reaction force to the rider, is used to realize a preferable pseudotrail. From the experiments, with the steer-by-wire bicycle it is confirmed that the controlled bicycle reproduce the same behavior as the bicycle with the offset at a speed of 10 km/h. From the observation, we conclude the effectiveness of the steering-assisted bicycle in improving postural stability is confirmed.

articleTitle: Buoyancy-Generating Snow Field Movement Mechanism Experimented on Pseudo-Snow Environment
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Mechatronics, Control and Robotics (ICMCR)
abstract: Currently, developments around robot mobility are very diverse. In disaster areas and other places where it is difficult for humans to walk, especially in places that are not flat, there are many kinds of research from various perspectives. Examples of previous studies include underwater movement and locations where it is difficult to obtain a stable posture, such as on the stony, sandy, and soft ground. On the other hand, relatively few studies on snow environments, such as snow damage sites, exist. This study aims to develop a mechanism for a mobile robot that can move stably on snow, which benefits investigation and supply rescue items at snow damage sites. This study investigates the mechanism by designing specialized wheels that gain buoyancy and traction force on snow. Also, we propose a pseudo-snow field that resembles the physical characteristics of snow, allowing snow-field mobile robots to experiment in warm environments.

articleTitle: Research on Labor Cost Adjustment Coefficient of Transmission Line Project Based on Improved SVM
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Mechatronics, Control and Robotics (ICMCR)
abstract: The effective management of labor costs is directly related to the project cost, project profits and the economic benefits of power construction enterprises, it also indirectly has an important impact on the quality and duration of construction projects. With the rise of labor cost, the overspending of labor cost in the cost of transmission line project has become more and more serious in recent years. This phenomenon causes a serious impact on the management of transmission line project. Therefore, the effective control of labor cost target is very important to improve the lean management level of transmission line project cost. In order to solve the price difference problem caused by labor cost fluctuation, this paper first identifies the key influencing factors of labor cost price difference. On this basis, the particle swarm optimization algorithm is used to optimize the parameters of support vector machine model. After that the calculation model of labor cost change adjustment coefficient is established. Finally, by using the actual data of labor cost change and influencing factors of power transmission project, this paper verifies the validity and feasibility of the model. Through the prediction of this model, we can effectively control the changes in labor costs, so as to calculate project costs more reasonably and optimize the management of transmission line projects.

articleTitle: Application of Genetic Algorithm in Global Optimization Design of Mechanical Engineering
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Mechatronics, Control and Robotics (ICMCR)
abstract: Compared with traditional mechanical design, global optimization design for mechanical engineering is a completely new concept. Its purpose is to improve the efficiency and quality of mechanical design. Therefore, this paper proposes a new kind of intelligent optimization method based on the basic theory of genetic algorithm. Then the Matlab software genetic algorithm toolbox is used to solve it. Then it is combined with a mechanical engineering global optimization design example to compare and analyze the sequential quadratic programming method and genetic algorithm. The results show that the volumes of the genetic algorithm and the traditional optimization method are 64.21% and 76.19%, respectively, suggesting that the process of genetic algorithm is efficient and can obtain good results. This paper presents an effective and innovative approach to global optimization design for mechanical engineering. The proposed genetic algorithm method is a promising method for enhancing the efficiency and quality of mechanical design. The findings of this study can be used as a reference for future research and development of global optimization design in mechanical engineering.

articleTitle: Digital Processing Techniques for PeruSat-1 Satellite Images for Estimation of the Surface Area of a Glacier
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Mechatronics, Control and Robotics (ICMCR)
abstract: This paper provides the estimation of the surface area of the Incachiriasca glacier located in the Historic Sanctuary of Machupicchu in Peru using digital processing techniques on satellite images obtained by the Peruvian satellite PeruSAT-1 and information from previous studies of the same area provided by the National Institute for Research on Glaciers and Mountain Ecosystems (INAIGEM) and National Service of Natural Areas Protected by the State (SERNANP). The development of this paper comprehends an alternative methodology in which, at first, analysis of traditional glacier monitoring techniques were used followed by spatial remote sensing with digital image processing and machine learning techniques. The estimated a surface area of the Incachiriasca glacier is 162,419.93 square meters and we can specify based on the analysis of an area of 54,457.65 square meters, which does not present distortions, that the glacier retreat is estimated is 1,940.83 square meters of retreat.

articleTitle: Postulating a Modular and Light-Weight Approach for Fuel Cell Stacking via Cobot Vacuum End-Effector Gripping
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Mechatronics, Control and Robotics (ICMCR)
abstract: In recent years, research in the field of fuel cells is gaining momentum. Leading automotive industries are investing in e-mobility. In fuel cell research, topics such as fuel cell durability, degradation phenomenon, catalyst performance enhancement, etc., are mainly researched upon. However, one fails to recognize the need for innovations in the area of assembly systems for the stacking process. In this paper, a modular approach referencing the gripping of bipolar plates and the membrane electrode assembly layers for the stacking process is postulated. A vacuum end-effector (VEE) gripper is innovated, designed, and manufactured using 3D printing methods. It is then tested in real-time at the maximum acceleration of the Cobot. The cycle time of assembly per unit cell achieved was 1.25s; for comparison, manual stacking per unit cell is averaged to approx. 8s. Therefore, huge potential savings in assembly time was denoted. Additionally, the benefit of using a vacuum end-effector gripper mitigates the particulate matter induced via manual handling. This prevents the early degradation of the fuel cell. The assembly technology and the demonstrator postulated in this paper integrates a complete loop of design, manufacturing, and assembly of the VEE gripping mechanism.
